---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Stress Year Fixed Charge Coverage
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(TS_MIN(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(TS_MIN(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Recurring commitments to creditors and shareholders must be paid every year, including bad ones, so the binding test is whether the firm's worst recent year of operating cash flow still cleared interest plus dividends; firms passing this test never face the choice between a dividend cut and distressed borrowing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Two independent design choices have each improved the coverage family — replacing maturing principal with recurring fixed charges (alpha 6.7%, t=4.16) and replacing mean cash flow with the worst-year draw (4.6% versus 5.2% on the same obligation set) — and this applies the tail-cash-flow choice to the superior obligation set. The consolidation is economically motivated rather than mechanical: fixed charges are precisely the claims that cannot be deferred in a weak year, so the tail statistic matters more here than it does for refinanceable principal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Funds From Operations Fixed Charge Coverage
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The economic content of fixed-charge coverage is whether the business throws off enough recurring internal funds to service its recurring claims, and funds from operations — income plus depreciation — measures that as well as the cash-flow statement does while being observable for far more firms and far earlier years.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every strong signal in this archive is capped near 0.08-0.09 coverage because oancf requires a modern cash-flow statement, and that thin sample is the most likely reason strong cross-sectional slopes translate into only moderate portfolio precision. Substituting ib+dp is not a cosmetic input swap but a deliberate sample-extension test: if the mechanism is real it should survive on a proxy that predates SFAS 95, and the wider cross-section should tighten the long-short alpha's standard error.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Coverage Of Total Annual Claims
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), dlc)), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), dlc), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm's true cash call in any year is the sum of contractual interest, expected dividends, and principal coming due; only cash flow exceeding the whole stack means the firm needs nothing from any capital provider, and partial coverage measures overstate autonomy by ignoring one claim class.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive has now tested the maturity claim alone (5.2% alpha) and the recurring claim alone (6.7% alpha) but never their union, so this determines whether the two obligation types carry independent information or whether the recurring-charge version already dominates. Because dlc is typically the largest term, this also acts as a diagnostic: if the union underperforms the recurring-only version, the priced mechanism is commitment burden rather than rollover risk, which redirects the final generations.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Discretionary Versus Contractual Charge Mix
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvt, xint), ADD(ADD(dvt, xint), 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Two cash generators with identical fixed-charge coverage differ fundamentally in flexibility: one whose charges are mostly dividends can suspend them at will, while one whose charges are mostly interest is contractually bound and defaults if it fails, so for equal cash generation the dividend-weighted firm carries a lower true risk that the market does not distinguish.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This shifts attention from the size of the commitment to its legal character, a dimension no archive signal has touched and one that is scale-free and therefore orthogonal to the coverage-level constructs. The composition leg is centered, so the cash-profitability rank only amplifies it, and the extremes are cash generators whose obligations are entirely cuttable versus cash generators locked into creditor payments.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Buybacks Out Of Post Commitment Surplus
EXPRESSION: RATIO(prstkc, ADD(ABS(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt))), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: A repurchase is credible evidence of underpriced cash generation only when it is funded from the cash left after servicing creditors and maintaining the dividend; scaling buybacks by that residual surplus, rather than by assets, identifies firms whose capital return is genuinely discretionary rather than financed by squeezing other claimants or by borrowing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Payout constructs in this archive consistently produced solid Fama-MacBeth slopes but near-zero FF5 alpha, and the plausible reason is that payout-to-assets is dominated by mature low-growth firms that RMW and CMA already price; deflating by discretionary surplus instead of by size changes what the sort ranks. This is the theme's core "return capital" idea rebuilt on the denominator that the last two generations showed to be the informative one.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Commitments Rising Faster Than Cash Generation
EXPRESSION: RATIO(DELTA(ADD(xint, dvt), 1), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that add to their recurring obligations — through higher interest bills or dividend increases — faster than their cash engine can support are pre-committing future cash they may not have; the added commitment looks like confidence at the announcement but raises the probability of a future cut or forced financing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive's short legs have been weak because they were built from gated products dominated by one leg, whereas this states the deterioration directly as a flow of new commitments per dollar of normalized cash generation. It is the dynamic counterpart of the fixed-charge mechanism rather than a first difference of the winning ratio, and it isolates the firms most exposed to an adverse cash-flow surprise, which should populate a clean short decile.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---CRITIQUE Stress Year Fixed Charge Coverage---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a mechanical 2x2 cell-fill — TS_MIN instead of MA on the already-tested recurring-charge coverage ratio, and the archive already contains both the MA/fixed-charge and TS_MIN/principal versions — so it is a cosmetic variant of the theme's best signal rather than a substantively different mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Funds From Operations Fixed Charge Coverage---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A single-input substitution on the archive's best signal, but the sample-extension motivation is legitimate and testable; note the stated diagnosis is weak, since non-oancf archive signals also sit at 0.10-0.13 coverage, implying the binding constraint is general annual-data alignment rather than SFAS 95, so expect only marginal coverage gain.

---CRITIQUE Coverage Of Total Annual Claims---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Adding dlc to the recurring-charge numerator is an additive union of two already-tested constructs in which dlc is numerically dominant, so the result will be close to a rescaled version of the existing near-term-debt coverage signal and carries low incremental information despite the reasonable ablation framing.

---CRITIQUE Discretionary Versus Contractual Charge Mix---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The legal-character-of-obligations dimension is genuinely untouched in the archive and scale-free, but it is heavily confounded with the well-known dividend-payer and low-leverage effects, and firms with neither dividends nor interest map to exactly the same value (0) as balanced firms, which will blur the middle of the sort.

---CRITIQUE Buybacks Out Of Post Commitment Surplus---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The expression contradicts its own hypothesis — the ABS in the denominator means the score is maximized when post-commitment surplus is near zero and decays as surplus grows, so the top decile is firms repurchasing while barely covering (or badly missing) their fixed charges, the opposite of "genuinely discretionary" buybacks.

---CRITIQUE Commitments Rising Faster Than Cash Generation---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The numerator sums two changes with opposite documented return signs — rising interest is a debt-growth/issuance proxy (negative) while dividend increases carry a well-known positive signal — so the legs will partly cancel and the expected negative sign is not cleanly implied by the expression.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Standard Deviations Of Fixed Charge Cushion
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(VOL(oancf, 5), 1)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: What determines whether recurring commitments become binding is the size of the cash cushion measured in units of the firm's own cash-flow uncertainty: a modest surplus is perfectly safe for a utility-like cash stream and perilously thin for a cyclical one, so the priced quantity is a distance-to-shortfall, not a scaled surplus.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Rather than filling the remaining cell of a mean/tail by principal/charges grid, this changes the deflator from firm size to firm risk, producing a Merton-style standardized cushion that ranks a stable firm with small surplus above a volatile firm with the same surplus. It is therefore not monotonically related to the existing coverage ratio, and it isolates the specific claim that cash-flow uncertainty, not scale, determines commitment risk.
REASONING: Winsorizing at 1% controls the low-volatility tail where the deflator is small, and the inputs are identical to the archive's best signal, so coverage stays near 0.08.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Debt Amortization Capacity From Free Cash
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), ABS(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)))))
HYPOTHESIS: The cash a firm keeps after interest and dividends is the only cash available to retire debt, so expressing that residual as a fraction of the debt stock measures how quickly the firm could extinguish creditor claims entirely; firms that could self-liquidate their debt in a few years hold real strategic optionality, while firms whose residual is trivial against their debt are permanently financed by lenders.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This avoids the additive-union problem the critic identified: dlc no longer sits in the numerator alongside much smaller recurring charges but appears in the denominator as part of the stock being amortized, so the measure asks a different question (speed of debt extinguishment) rather than re-stating annual coverage. The bounded [-1, 1] form handles firms with negative residual cash correctly, and it links the recurring-charge mechanism that produced the archive's best alpha to the debt-stock dimension that the coverage family has only measured as a maturity calendar.
REASONING: All inputs are already in the archive's sample, so coverage remains near 0.08-0.09.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Repurchases Backed By Discretionary Surplus
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(prstkc, at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A repurchase is credible evidence of underpriced cash generation only when the firm also has substantial cash left after servicing creditors and maintaining its dividend; buybacks by firms with no discretionary surplus are financed by borrowing or by starving other claims and carry no positive information.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This removes the ABS pathology the critic identified — the surplus now enters monotonically as its own standardized leg, so larger surplus always raises the score and the top decile is firms with both a big post-commitment cushion and large repurchases. The conjunction is also the sharpest available test of the theme's central claim, since the long leg is exactly "profitable firm returning capital it can demonstrably spare" and the short leg is firms failing on whichever dimension is weaker.
REASONING: Both legs are continuous industry z-scores of quantities already available in the archive's sample, so no coverage is sacrificed relative to the payout constructs.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Rising Interest Burden Against Post Dividend Cash
EXPRESSION: RATIO(DELTA(xint, 1), ADD(ABS(MA(SUB(oancf, dvt), 3)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: An increase in the contractual interest bill is an unambiguous tightening of the claim on future cash, and it is dangerous in proportion to how little cash remains after the firm has paid the dividend it is reluctant to cut; firms whose interest burden is growing fast relative to post-dividend cash are pre-committing cash they may not have.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: The critic correctly noted that dividend increases and interest increases carry opposite documented signs, so the revised numerator keeps only the contractual component while the discretionary dividend moves to the denominator, where a larger payout correctly reduces the cash available to absorb the higher interest. The construction now has one clean direction — more interest growth and less post-dividend cash both push the score up and returns down — making the negative sign an implication of the expression rather than an assertion.
REASONING: Using oancf net of dividends as the deflator also distinguishes this from the level-coverage family, since two firms with identical coverage differ here according to how much of their cash is already spoken for.
